items.title: AB-3028 CAR-T Cell Therapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing AB-3028, a new type of engineered immune cell therapy (CAR-T), in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting patients to evaluate both safety and effectiveness. This represents a novel approach using programmable immune cells to target advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large phase 3 study tests whether adding niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard abiraterone and prednisone therapy improves outcomes in metastatic prostate cancer. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients but remains active. Combining PARP inhibitors with hormone therapy represents an important treatment strategy for advanced disease.

items.title: Pasritamig Plus Docetaxel Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial compares pasritamig combined with docetaxel chemotherapy versus docetaxel alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The goal is to determine if adding pasritamig extends the time before disease progression on scans. Pasritamig is a novel T-cell redirecting therapy targeting a prostate-specific protein.

items.title: Mevrometostat for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study is testing mevrometostat, an epigenetic drug that blocks a protein called EZH2, in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after prior treatments. Part 3 is actively recruiting and includes combination testing with enzalutamide. This represents a novel approach targeting cancer cell gene regulation.

items.title: Pasritamig Phase 3 Trial in Late-Line Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 study evaluates whether pasritamig extends survival compared to placebo in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have received multiple prior treatments. This trial targets patients with heavily pre-treated disease who have limited remaining options. Pasritamig is a T-cell redirecting antibody.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial tests whether adding mevrometostat to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't yet received hormone-blocking drugs. This represents testing a novel epigenetic therapy in earlier-stage metastatic disease before resistance develops.

items.title: Cabozantinib and Atezolizumab Phase 2 for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 2 trial tests the combination of cabozantinib (a targeted therapy) with atezolizumab (an immunotherapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if this combination can shrink tumors by blocking growth signals while activating the immune system against cancer cells.

items.title: Pasritamig Combination Therapy Phase 1 Trial
items.summary: This recruiting early-stage trial is testing pasritamig in combination with other cancer drugs for metastatic prostate cancer. The study will identify safe and effective dose combinations and regimens. This represents exploratory work to find optimal ways to use this T-cell redirecting therapy with other treatments.

items.title: Radium-223 With M3814 and Immunotherapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 1/2 trial compares radium-223 radiation therapy alone versus combinations with M3814 (a DNA repair blocker) and/or avelumab (immunotherapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone metastases. The study tests whether adding drugs that enhance radiation effects or boost immunity improves outcomes.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 study tests whether combining mevrometostat with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who haven't received certain hormone therapies. This large trial targets patients whose cancer has progressed despite testosterone suppression.

items.title: Sacituzumab Govitecan Phase 2 for Advanced CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 study investigates sacituzumab govitecan, an antibody-drug conjugate, in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose disease progressed on newer hormone therapies like enzalutamide or abiraterone. The trial is no longer recruiting but remains active. This drug delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells.

items.title: INV-9956 Phase 1/2 for Advanced Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting early-stage study evaluates INV-9956, a new investigational drug, for safety and anti-tumor activity in advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial will determine appropriate doses and assess whether the drug shows promise in shrinking tumors or controlling disease.

items.title: Hormone Therapy Duration With Radiation for Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 2 trial studies whether adding abiraterone to standard radiation and hormone therapy improves quality of life in men with oligometastatic prostate cancer (cancer spread to only a few sites). Patients receive either standard treatment or standard treatment plus abiraterone for 8-9 months.

items.title: Talazoparib Safety Analysis in TALAPRO-2 Trial
items.summary: This paper analyzes the relationship between drug exposure levels and safety outcomes for talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer from the TALAPRO-2 trial. Understanding these relationships helps optimize dosing to balance effectiveness and side effects.

items.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Advances in Cancer Treatment
items.summary: This review discusses emerging radiopharmaceutical therapies in oncology, including their role in treating various cancers. Radiopharmaceuticals like radium-223 and lutetium-177-PSMA are increasingly important for advanced prostate cancer. The paper covers recent advances, ongoing challenges, and future directions in this rapidly evolving field.

items.title: Optimizing Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This educational review from the American Society of Clinical Oncology provides guidance on optimizing treatment approaches for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The paper synthesizes current evidence and best practices to help clinicians make informed treatment decisions for this advanced disease stage.

items.title: Novel Therapies Beyond Hormone Blockade for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This review examines new therapeutic strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that go beyond traditional hormone-blocking approaches. It discusses emerging treatment options and mechanisms that may overcome resistance to standard hormone therapies, providing insights into the evolving treatment landscape.

items.title: Overcoming PARP Inhibitor Resistance Through Drug Combinations
items.summary: This review explores innovative drug combinations to overcome resistance to PARP inhibitors in cancer treatment, including prostate cancer. As PARP inhibitors become standard for certain prostate cancers, understanding and addressing resistance mechanisms through combination approaches is increasingly important for maintaining treatment effectiveness.

items.title: PARP Inhibition With Vitamin C Shows Synergy in CRPC
items.summary: This study demonstrates that combining PARP inhibitors with pharmacological doses of vitamin C (ascorbate) produces synergistic anti-cancer effects in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The research suggests a potential strategy to enhance PARP inhibitor effectiveness through this combination approach.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a new dual-action drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This novel compound addresses a key resistance mechanism that limits the effectiveness of AKT inhibitors alone, potentially offering a new treatment strategy.

items.title: International Analysis of Prostate Cancer Drug Reimbursement and Clinical Benefit
items.summary: This study analyzed reimbursement rates and clinical benefit ratings for prostate, kidney, and bladder cancer drugs across eight countries including Canada and major European nations. The analysis found varying reimbursement rates and examined relationships between drug approval characteristics, survival benefits, and coverage decisions.
